claims.claim: In-batch negatives are a training technique in DPR.
Negative passages are taken from other questions in the same mini-batch.
Each question in a batch of B has its own positive passage.
The model computes a similarity matrix S = Q P^T of size B x B.
Every question is paired with every passage in the batch.
The pair (qi, pi) where i = j is a positive example.
Pairs (qi, pj) where i != j are negative examples.
This creates B x (B - 1) negative pairs per batch.
The approach reuses negative examples already present in the batch.
It increases the number of training instances compared to standard 1-of-N training.
In-batch negative training improves retrieval accuracy.
Accuracy improves as batch size grows.
It leverages gold negatives from the same batch.
